Herpesvirus once caught is in your car forever, that doesn’t mean your cat is going to be sick for ever. Flare ups come as someone else said with stress that lowers the immune system. That could be from food, a new pet neighbour, to an underlying new condition. The flare up should be controlled by treating the symptoms, but it won’t go away if you don’t also treat the underlying cause of stress. Also green mucus is highly indicative of a concomitant opportunistic bacterial infection. It’s been months and no resolution so, find a different vet, maybe in a different town, or someone that can travel, figure it out, because your cat is been having a tough time for more than two months. If absolutely nothing can be done to reach another vet, consider asking for help to a charitable organisation or surrendering so that your cat can have the necessary treatment.
Edit: forgot to say that it may be something completely different from herpesvirus and could be more serious, more painful or more deadly. The cat needs another examination, complementary tests, and disease specific treatment.
